title: Biological reconstruction of foveal cones, RPE, and their blood supply

concept.text: The proposed innovation is to rebuild the living tissue responsible for sharp central vision after its light-sensing cells have died. A successful treatment would establish a durable mosaic of cone photoreceptors in a degenerated human macula, give those cells functional light-sensitive outer segments, and connect them appropriately to surviving host bipolar cells so that their signals can enter the existing visual pathway.

The cones would also need adequate support from the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), the underlying Bruch’s membrane, and the choriocapillaris blood supply. The RPE helps transport nutrients from the choroid and remove photoreceptor debris. Reconstruction therefore concerns a functioning tissue system, rather than simply placing new light-sensitive cells in the eye. Which supporting layers require replacement or repair would depend on the recipient’s lesion; the supplied evidence does not establish that every patient needs all of them rebuilt.

The intended route could involve transplantation, regeneration within the eye, or a combination. Its defining outcome would be biological phototransduction and useful central vision attributable to reconstructed tissue. Survival of an RPE graft alone would establish a narrower achievement, while an electronic implant would provide a different mechanism of vision restoration.

significance.text: Geographic atrophy destroys macular photoreceptors, and advanced inherited retinal diseases can also cause irreversible retinal cell loss. Existing approaches include anti-VEGF treatment for neovascular AMD and complement inhibition intended to slow geographic atrophy. Durable reconstruction would add the ability to repair some central vision loss after cells have died, rather than relying solely on preserving remaining tissue or substituting an artificial signal. The supplied evidence does not document an achieved reconstruction of a naturally functioning human fovea.

The disease burden makes that possibility consequential. In a news release dated 5 May 2013, NEI described advanced AMD as the leading cause of blindness in the United States; this is a historical attribution, not an updated ranking for every population. The supplied WHO fact sheet, dated 10 February 2026, attributes approximately 8 million cases of distance vision impairment or blindness to AMD. That number describes disease burden and cannot be treated as the population eligible for foveal reconstruction.

Conditional impact synthesis: clinically useful reading under natural light would demonstrate an important new capacity for biological central-vision repair. It would not, by itself, establish normal color discrimination, adaptation to changing illumination, normal foveal resolution, or restoration of the entire visual field. Describing central vision loss as a repairable tissue injury would be justified only for the diseases, lesions, and functional outcomes actually demonstrated. Extension to widespread retinal degeneration would remain a further possibility requiring additional evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is coordinated survival and functional integration of replacement or regenerated cones in a diseased human macula. NEI describes humans as having little, if any, capacity to replace lost retinal neurons. Producing retinal cells is therefore only an intermediate step: the cells must persist, form functioning outer segments, and establish appropriate connections with host circuitry. Anatomical survival without usable signal transmission would leave the main reconstruction goal unmet.

A second barrier is sustaining the reconstructed tissue. Adequate RPE function and metabolic support from the choroid must accompany the cones, with repair of damaged support structures where necessary. Immune rejection and resource-intensive cell production are documented challenges. The original research also identifies scarring as a possible obstacle, but the supplied review does not directly substantiate a specific graft-scarring mechanism or its frequency; it remains a concern to investigate rather than an established explanation for failure.

Engineering synthesis: the treatment would have to coordinate cell identity, spatial organization, delivery, tissue support, and circuit integration in the same recipient. It would also need to establish which downstream retinal pathways remain usable in advanced disease. Success in a small central graft would not automatically solve manufacturing, delivery, immune management, or integration across a much larger retinal area.

current_state.text: NEI’s AGI projects describe work on survival and integration of regenerated retinal cells, including photoreceptors, against the background of very limited natural neuronal replacement in humans. Cavaleri and colleagues’ 2025 review characterizes visual improvements across neurorestoration approaches as generally modest and notes reliance on small preliminary studies and potential bias. That assessment is a broad expert judgment, not a standardized quantitative comparison with normal macular vision. Its included studies extend through September 2025; the supplied extraction is truncated in the references, although the relevant narrative passages were available to the reviewer.

The supplied research attributes to Heier and colleagues’ OAKS and DERBY report, dated 21 October 2023, approximately 16–22% less geographic-atrophy growth with pegcetacoplan at 24 months and no difference in the key secondary visual-function endpoints at that time. These numerical and endpoint details remain unconfirmed within the supplied evidence because the retained article copy contains only redirect text. They should be read as reported research details pending verification, not as disproven findings. The broader distinction between slowing atrophy and rebuilding lost photoreceptors is supported by the supplied PRIMA manuscript.

The supplied research describes Rao and colleagues’ report, dated 6 November 2025, as an adult RPE-stem-cell graft study involving six people, with low-dose safety findings and a mean gain of 21.67 letters at 12 months in the three worse-seeing eyes. It also describes the trial as not powered for efficacy and as not rebuilding cones. The retained source contains only redirect text, so the participant count, safety interpretation, subgroup result, statistical-power statement, and cone-reconstruction conclusion cannot be confirmed here. Even if the reported visual gain is verified, an RPE intervention would require additional evidence before it could establish reconstruction of a functional cone mosaic.

The supplied research attributes to Hirami and colleagues’ report, dated 7 December 2023, survival of allogeneic retinal-organoid sheets for two years in two people with retinitis pigmentosa, with a possible light-response change in one participant. The retained article copy contains only redirect text, leaving those trial-specific details unconfirmed. The reported distinction remains scientifically important: persistence of transplanted tissue and a possible light response would be partial achievements, rather than evidence of reconstructed foveal reading vision.

A clearer demonstrated comparator is the PRIMA prosthesis in the supplied Holz and colleagues author manuscript, published online on 20 October 2025. Its pixels convert projected near-infrared light into electrical stimulation of surviving bipolar cells. Mean unenhanced prosthetic acuity was 1.32 ± 0.16 logMAR, approximately Snellen 20/417, consistent with the sampling limit of its 100 µm pixels. At 12 months, 26 of 32 assessed participants improved by at least 0.2 logMAR relative to baseline; 38 participants had been enrolled. The system-assisted testing allowed adjustable zoom and brightness, so that improvement should not be equated with native implant resolution. The system uses camera-equipped glasses and near-infrared projection. These results demonstrate electronic substitution, not biological cone replacement. The supplied review assessed the main manuscript prose; its figures and linked supplements were not inspected.

The supplied research also cites Ho’s 2024 IOVS conference abstract 2137 for approximately 0.3 logMAR improvement from count-fingers baselines after optogenetic bipolar-cell therapy. No abstract text was captured, so the magnitude, baseline characterization, and trial details cannot be confirmed from the supplied materials. This is a conference-level report in the research record, not a reviewed full clinical report here. The record does not establish whether a full peer-reviewed RESTORE report was available by 1 November 2026.

The evidence supports a landscape of partial biological approaches and demonstrated prosthetic function, while leaving the integrated reconstruction goal unachieved in the supplied record. It does not establish a complete treatment or approval inventory as of 1 November 2026. Although the supplied primary PRIMA manuscript extends beyond the review’s September 2025 study cutoff, the empty freshness record prevents a confident claim that all subsequent developments have been captured.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: in patients with fovea-involving geographic atrophy or an end-stage macular dystrophy and suitable surviving downstream circuitry, a cell or regeneration therapy would produce photoreceptor outer segments, a measurable cone response attributable to the reconstructed tissue, and clinically useful reading under natural light without an electronic implant or intensifying goggles. Acuity, reading performance, illumination conditions, safety outcomes, and a multiyear durability interval should be defined prospectively. These are proposed evaluation criteria, not established consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal and anatomical evidence: demonstrate benefit against an appropriate control, using an untreated fellow eye only where its disease course and other characteristics make it a suitable comparator. Combine functional outcomes with evidence of graft or regenerated-cell persistence, host-circuit integration, and adequate RPE and metabolic support. Functional improvement alone would not establish every anatomical component named in the concept, while anatomical survival alone would not establish useful vision. RPE survival and prosthetic pixels would each fall short of the integrated biological outcome.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed causal and anatomical evidence

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: reproduce the outcome across patients and independent clinical teams, with consistent manufacturing or regeneration methods and follow-up sufficient to assess durability and immune complications. Report the lesions, retained circuitry, treatment burden, and safety conditions under which benefit occurs. Claims about restored color vision or adaptation require dedicated tests. Successful finite trials would establish breadth within the tested population and conditions, rather than universal applicability across macular diseases or proof that full-field replacement is feasible.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based distinction: OPH-11, “Prevention of progression from early or intermediate AMD to late AMD,” addresses disease progression before the advanced tissue-loss state targeted here. OPH-07, “One programmable repair for many photoreceptor and RPE gene defects,” addresses genetic repair. Its overlap with OPH-02 could include protecting or correcting cells used in reconstruction, but gene correction in surviving native cells would not itself replace an already lost cone mosaic. These relationships follow the supplied titles and research framing; detailed definitions of OPH-07 and OPH-11 were not independently established.

Roster-based distinction: OPH-08, “Reperfusion of established retinal capillary dropout,” overlaps with the need for adequate blood supply, but retinal capillary reperfusion and reconstruction of choriocapillaris support beneath the RPE are different anatomical targets. OPH-01, “Retinotopic reconnection of retinal ganglion cell axons to brain targets,” concerns the output pathway beyond the photoreceptors and bipolar cells. OPH-10, “Arrest of glaucomatous ganglion-cell death when pressure is not the lever,” concerns preservation of that downstream neuronal population. These capabilities could matter when damage extends beyond the outer retina, but none alone establishes foveal cone reconstruction.

Roster-based distinction: OPH-05, “Patterned vision from the brain when the eye cannot send signals,” seeks visual function through a different intervention site. OPH-09, “Reopening of the human visual critical period,” concerns neural plasticity, which could be relevant to learning to use restored retinal signals but would not itself supply missing retinal tissue. PRIMA and optogenetic bipolar-cell approaches likewise illustrate alternative routes to visual function rather than completion of OPH-02.

Roster-based distinction: OPH-03, “Reversal of established cataract without removing the lens,” and OPH-04, “A manufactured cornea that clears vascularized stromal opacity,” target optical barriers in front of the retina. OPH-06, “A closed-loop control that sets axial eye growth,” targets ocular growth. They address different causes of impaired vision and remain separate innovations. Full-field photoreceptor replacement in widespread retinitis pigmentosa shares OPH-02’s underlying reconstruction biology, while adding substantial scale, delivery, manufacturing, and integration requirements.

change_log.change: Preserved OPH-02 and its original title while defining completion as integrated biological central-vision restoration.
change_log.reason: The evidence limitations affect individual assertions, not the coherence or identity of the innovation.

change_log.change: Made replacement of RPE, Bruch’s membrane, and choriocapillaris dependent on the recipient lesion.
change_log.reason: Adequate support is necessary, but the supplied evidence does not show that every patient requires replacement of every supporting layer.

change_log.change: Replaced exhaustive claims about current drugs and approved reconstruction treatments with a statement about what the supplied evidence documents.
change_log.reason: The record does not establish a complete treatment inventory through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Corrected the WHO fact-sheet date to 10 February 2026 and retained the 8 million figure as AMD-attributed distance vision impairment or blindness.
change_log.reason: Disease burden does not establish eligibility for foveal reconstruction.

change_log.change: Retained the 2013 NEI blindness statement with its historical date.
change_log.reason: The source supports that attribution, not an updated epidemiological ranking.

change_log.change: Preserved the research’s Heier, Rao, Hirami, and Ho numerical details as explicitly unconfirmed reports, alongside their access limitations.
change_log.reason: Redirect-only copies and an uncaptured abstract prevent confirmation but do not demonstrate that the reported results are false.

change_log.change: Separated PRIMA’s unenhanced implant acuity from system-assisted improvement and added variability, enrolled and assessed denominators, and testing conditions.
change_log.reason: Pixel-limited resolution and performance with adjustable zoom and brightness measure different aspects of prosthetic vision.

change_log.change: Limited the interpretation of Cavaleri and colleagues’ review and preserved its extraction and study-coverage boundaries.
change_log.reason: Its assessment is a broad expert judgment based partly on small preliminary studies, with coverage through September 2025.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to address attribution, appropriate controls, reproducibility, tissue support, durability, and functional boundaries.
change_log.reason: Reading gains alone would not establish all anatomical components, normal color vision, adaptation, or universal applicability.

change_log.change: Expanded related-concept distinctions using the supplied roster without merging entries.
change_log.reason: Prevention, genetic repair, vascular repair, downstream reconnection, optical repair, and visual substitution address different capabilities.

unresolved_issues: The Heier, Rao, and Hirami numerical findings and trial-specific interpretations require article or abstract content beyond the retained redirect text; Ho’s abstract was not captured.

The recommendation to remove the unconfirmed trial details was not adopted wholesale. They were retained as clearly qualified reports to preserve useful quantitative research detail without presenting it as verified.
The record cannot establish whether a full peer-reviewed RESTORE report or other material developments were available by 1 November 2026; the supplied freshness record is empty.
The lesion-specific need to replace RPE, Bruch’s membrane, or choriocapillaris, and the minimum surviving downstream circuitry needed for benefit, remain to be determined.
The specific importance and mechanism of graft scarring are not directly substantiated by the supplied evidence.
Clinically useful acuity, reading performance, acceptable treatment burden, and the required multiyear durability interval remain proposed criteria needing prospective operational definitions.
The eligible treatment population cannot be inferred from WHO’s AMD burden estimate, and detailed definitions of related roster entries extend beyond the supplied titles and research framing.
